80	Initial task ownership
81	----------------------
82	A fleet can be created mid-work: a robot may already name its current task
83	with a remaining route, and a task may already be assigned or even loaded.
84	Construction validates these bindings up front instead of discovering them
85	while stepping. Every robot that names a task must name one that exists, is
86	still unfinished and is assigned back to that robot; every unfinished task
87	that names an owner must name an existing robot whose current task it is, and
88	a task with the goods collected may never lack that owner. One robot is
89	therefore never claimed by two unfinished tasks, and a robot may never be
90	bound to a completed task. A finished task is a fixed historical record and
91	must carry both the picked-up mark and the historical robot that finished it:
92	``assigned_robot`` of ``None`` means the record is missing, not an anonymous
93	completion, and the mark is never presumed -- not even when the task's pickup
94	point and dropoff are the same cell. Finished tasks only retain *historical*
95	ownership: their recorded robot need not be idle or name them back, may
96	already work a new task, may have finished several tasks, and may even be
97	absent from the fleet, so history never occupies a robot or enters new task
98	assignment. Unassigned, not-yet-collected tasks simply wait -- including ones
99	no robot can currently reach -- and are not an ownership error. Conflicts
100	raise :class:`ValueError` naming the robot or task and the contradiction
101	involved; nothing is rebound, unassigned or dropped, and the caller's objects
102	are left untouched. The very same ownership and completed-history rules
103	govern checkpoint loading, so a completion record one entry point accepts
104	can never be a record the other cannot reload.
105	
106	Every task's pickup point and dropoff is validated with the very same strict
107	coordinate rule as robot positions (:func:`_as_cell`): each must be a list or
108	tuple holding exactly two plain integers, and the two spellings may be mixed
109	freely within one task and across one batch. A boolean is never an integer
110	here -- not even ``True`` for a 1-coordinate -- and a float is refused even
111	when it equals an integer value such as ``1.0``; strings, nulls, scalars,
112	missing components, extra components and anything that is not a coordinate
113	pair all raise :class:`ValueError` naming the task id and whether its pickup
114	or its dropoff is at fault -- nothing is rounded, padded or coerced into a
115	pair, so a fleet can never accept a task that its own checkpoint loading
116	would later reject. An accepted point is normalized to a fresh integer tuple
117	(``[1, 0]`` and ``(1, 0)`` therefore name one cell: a robot can neither miss
118	a pickup nor fail a delivery merely because the containers differ), and the
119	copy means a caller that keeps mutating its original coordinate lists after
120	construction can never change the created fleet. The rule covers every task
121	regardless of state -- waiting for assignment, already assigned and heading
122	to pickup, carrying the goods, and finished historical records alike. Like
123	position normalization, the points commit nothing until the whole batch
124	(positions, ownership, routes and all task points) has passed: a failure on a
125	later task point, robot route or binding leaves every earlier task holding
126	its original pickup/dropoff containers and every flag, binding, route and
127	mileage exactly as passed in. Coordinate validity and current reachability
128	are deliberately separate judgements: a well-formed task no robot can
129	currently reach simply keeps waiting, and a loaded task whose pickup cell has
130	since been closed keeps the goods and its owner -- neither is a coordinate
131	error, and selection order, planning, obstacle handling and completion
132	history behave exactly as before. Checkpoints keep their integer coordinate
133	arrays and strict loading rules unchanged -- no format bump and no
134	relaxation.
135	
136	Every robot's starting position is validated with the very same strict
137	coordinate rule its route waypoints use (:func:`_as_cell`): it must be a list
138	or tuple holding exactly two plain integers, and the two spellings may be
139	mixed freely within one batch. A boolean is never an integer here, and floats,
140	strings, missing or extra components and anything that is not a coordinate
141	pair all raise :class:`ValueError` naming the robot and its offending starting
142	position -- nothing is rounded, coerced or padded into a pair. An accepted
143	position is normalized to a fresh integer tuple (``[0, 0]`` and ``(0, 0)``
144	therefore create identical fleets that move and receive tasks identically),
145	and the copy means a caller that keeps mutating its original list after
146	construction can never change the created fleet. Positions must lie inside
147	the map and outside every obstacle, and no two robots may start on the same
148	cell: the comparison is made on the normalized coordinate values, so a list
149	and a tuple naming one cell still collide, and the error names both robots.
150	This covers every robot regardless of task state -- unbound, task-executing
151	and preset-route robots alike -- so a batch can never succeed by ignoring one
152	robot. Like the route check, position normalization commits nothing until the
153	entire batch (positions, ownership and routes) has passed: a failure on a
154	later robot's route or task binding leaves every earlier robot's original
155	position object, remaining route and task binding exactly as passed in.
156	
157	Every robot's remaining route is also validated as a walk on the given map,
158	whether or not the robot is bound to a task, and direct construction and
159	checkpoint recovery run the *same* :func:`_validate_route_walk` check, so the
160	walking rule is maintained in exactly one place. The route omits the robot's
161	current cell, so a non-empty route must begin with an up/down/left/right
162	neighbour of that cell and every later waypoint must be one orthogonal step
163	from the previous one; each waypoint must be in bounds and free of obstacles.
164	Diagonal steps, multi-cell jumps, two identical consecutive waypoints and a
165	first waypoint equal to the current position are all rejected, and waypoints
166	must be two plain integers (never booleans) in a list or tuple, with wrong
167	lengths or element types raising :class:`ValueError` rather than leaking
168	unpacking or hashing errors. Empty routes stay legal; a route need not be
169	shortest and may revisit cells. A route crossing another robot's current cell,
170	or several robots planning through the same cell, is not an error -- those
171	traffic conflicts are settled during execution. The direct interface keeps
172	its existing acceptance of a bound route's pickup/dropoff ordering and end
173	point; checkpoint loading additionally keeps its own stricter route checks
174	(including the task completion rules), its format and the map-paused
175	behaviour, under which a paused robot resumes with an empty route.
176	
177	Direct construction always judges every waypoint against the map handed to
178	it, so a route crossing an initial obstacle is rejected no matter the robot's
179	task state. Checkpoint recovery owns exactly one relaxation, and only for a
180	version 2 document: a robot with no bound task keeps its remaining preset
181	waypoints when a later map edit closes the cell ahead -- it simply waits
182	before it -- so such a waypoint may be blocked on the saved map provided it
183	was traversable on the base map, some recorded change net-closes it and it is
184	still closed at save time. The set of cells this can possibly cover is
185	derived from the already validated ``base_grid`` plus ``map_changes``, never
186	from the route itself: a base-map obstacle and any blocked cell the history
187	cannot explain stay rejected, version 1 files (which carry no history) keep
188	the old rule, and a task-bound robot never qualifies. Out-of-bounds,
189	malformed and non-adjacent waypoints are rejected for every robot either
190	way. After reopening, the restored robot keeps driving the same cells in the
191	same order: waiting neither consumes a waypoint nor adds mileage, and the
192	route is never replanned into a shortcut.
193	
194	Checkpoint file format
195	----------------------
196	``save_checkpoint`` writes versioned, UTF-8 encoded JSON. The current format
197	version is ``2``; version ``1`` files remain readable.
198	
199	``version``
200	    Integer format version (``1`` or ``2``).
201	``grid``
202	    ``{"width": int, "height": int, "obstacles": [[x, y], ...]}`` describing
203	    the map dimensions and every currently blocked cell.
204	``tick``
205	    Non-negative integer: the number of ticks already executed. Saving and
206	    loading never advance this value.
207	``robots``
208	    List of robot states, each
209	    ``{"robot_id": str, "position": [x, y], "route": [[x, y], ...],
210	    "task_id": str | null, "distance_travelled": int}``. ``route`` holds the
211	    remaining waypoints after ``position`` (empty for a paused robot). For a
212	    taskless robot the route may head into a cell the change history has
213	    closed and the saved grid still shows blocked: the robot is simply waiting
214	    there with its preset waypoints intact, and loading restores that wait.
215	``tasks``
216	    List of task states, each
217	    ``{"task_id": str, "pickup": [x, y], "dropoff": [x, y],
218	    "assigned_robot": str | null, "picked_up": bool, "completed": bool}``.
219	    Completed tasks keep their historical ``assigned_robot``: a task saved as
220	    completed must also be marked picked up and name the robot that finished
221	    it (never null), and loading rejects a record missing either half with the
222	    same rule direct fleet construction enforces.
223	``replay``
224	    Ordered event list. Tick events are numbered consecutively from ``1``
225	    through ``tick`` and have the shape
226	    ``{"type": "tick", "tick": int, "moved": [robot_id, ...],
227	    "robots": {robot_id: [x, y], ...}, "completed": [task_id, ...]}``.
228	    ``completed`` is the cumulative set of tasks finished by the end of that
229	    tick: entries must name checkpoint tasks without repeats within one frame,
230	    a recorded completion must survive every later frame, and the final
231	    frame's set must equal the tasks saved with ``completed: true``.
232	    Map-change events sit between ticks (or after the last tick) and look like
233	    ``{"type": "map_change", "tick": int, "sequence": int,
234	    "added": [[x, y], ...], "removed": [[x, y], ...]}``. When ``tick`` is
235	    non-zero the final tick event's robot positions must match the current
236	    robot positions.
237	``map_changes`` (version 2 only)
238	    List mirroring the replay map-change events in the same order:
239	    ``{"tick": int, "sequence": int, "added": [...], "removed": [...]}``.
240	``base_grid`` (version 2 only)
241	    ``{"width", "height", "obstacles"}`` describing the map before any runtime
242	    edit. Replaying ``map_changes`` against it must reproduce the saved current
243	    ``grid``.
244	``traffic_waits`` (optional)
245	    List of ``{"robot_id": str, "blocked_by": [str, ...], "ticks": int}``
246	    entries recording how many consecutive ticks each robot has been held up
247	    purely by other robots. Absent in older files, which load with every
248	    wait counter at zero. Each entry must agree with the saved layout: the
249	    robot needs a remaining route and ``blocked_by`` must name exactly the
250	    robot occupying its next route cell -- a next cell nobody occupies, a
251	    listed blocker parked elsewhere, or extra names beside the real blocker
252	    all reject the document.
253	
254	Version 1 documents store tick frames without a ``type`` field and have no
255	``map_changes`` or ``base_grid`` key; they load with their grid taken as the
256	baseline, as if no map edit ever happened.
257	
258	The ordinary-tick-frame rules both versions share -- the replay container is
259	a list, every frame is an object, and tick frames are numbered consecutively
260	from 1 with a well-formed payload -- are owned by the single shared
261	:meth:`FleetSimulator._iter_replay_events` scan, so they are maintained in
262	exactly one place. Each version keeps its own handling on top: version 1
263	rejects non-tick frames and fills in the missing ``type`` on a copy, while
264	version 2 dispatches event types and enforces its map-change ordering.
265	
266	Both map definitions are validated by the single shared
267	:meth:`FleetSimulator._load_map_definition` rule -- positive integer
268	dimensions, an obstacle list of integer ``[x, y]`` pairs inside the map --
269	with wording that names the map at fault, so a format or value rule is
270	maintained in exactly one place while each map keeps its own contents. The
271	cross-definition constraints (matching dimensions and a history that replays
272	``base_grid`` onto ``grid``) are checked separately and remain distinct
273	rejection reasons from a malformed definition.
274	
275	Loading performs strict validation: malformed JSON, missing or wrongly typed
276	fields, unsupported versions, duplicate or inconsistent entities, out of
277	bounds/obstructed positions and routes, non-adjacent route steps, ownership
278	mismatches, routes that cannot finish the robot's bound task, traffic waits
279	that contradict the saved robot positions and remaining routes, broken replay
280	or map-change history, a completion history that contradicts the saved task
281	states, and a history that does not reproduce the saved grid all raise
282	:class:`ValueError`.
283	
284	The single route-walk exception recovery allows is a preset-route robot that
285	is waiting out a dynamic closure. In a version 2 file a robot without a bound
286	task may keep waypoints that are blocked on the saved grid when the base map
287	had the cell open and the recorded change history explains its current,
288	still-effective closure (a cell closed and reopened before the save is open
289	again and therefore never covered). Such a robot was produced by normal
290	running -- closing a cell never strips a taskless robot of its remaining
291	route, the robot just waits before the cell -- so recovery restores it as is
292	and it drives on, same cells, same order, once the cell reopens. The
293	exemption cannot reach anything else: direct fleet construction has no
294	history and rejects routes through initial obstacles, a blocked waypoint the
295	history cannot account for (including every blocked waypoint in a version 1
296	document) is still rejected, and robots bound to a task never qualify --
297	their routes are replanned or their tasks paused at edit time and load under
298	the unchanged task rules. A robot standing on an obstacle and an out-of-map,
299	malformed or non-adjacent waypoint are rejected regardless of task state.
300	
301	A task-bound route is judged against the task's pickup state, not just for
302	walkability. For every assigned, unfinished task that is not paused by map
303	unreachability, a non-empty remaining route must end at the dropoff, and when
304	the goods are not yet collected and the robot is not already standing on the
305	pickup cell, the route must still pass through that pickup cell -- passing the
306	dropoff early changes nothing as long as the route later collects and returns,
307	and avoidance detours need not match a replanned shortest route. An empty
308	route is accepted only when a loaded robot already stands at the dropoff, or
309	when position, pickup and dropoff all coincide; paused tasks keep their
310	empty-route exemption, and unassigned or completed tasks are not checked.
311	
312	The recorded movement history is checked for physical plausibility, not just
313	for a matching final frame. In every tick frame each robot must stand on a
314	cell that is in bounds and traversable on the map of that moment, no two
315	robots may end a tick on the same cell, and from the second frame on a robot
316	may only have waited or stepped one orthogonal cell (two robots cannot swap
317	cells within one tick; following a robot into the cell it just vacated is
318	fine). A frame's ``moved`` list must reference current fleet robots without
319	duplicates and, whenever a previous frame exists, must name exactly the
320	robots whose positions changed, in any order. Version 2 map changes are
321	applied in their recorded order after the tick they are stamped on, so a
322	robot may be recorded in a cell that is closed later, may not appear in a
323	cell before it opens, and no change may add an obstacle onto a cell a tick
324	frame shows occupied -- not even when a later change of the same tick removes
325	it. Filesystem and permission failures propagate as :class:`OSError`.
326	"""

345	def _is_int(value: object) -> bool:
346	    """JSON booleans are ints in Python; checkpoints treat them as wrong."""
347	    return isinstance(value, int) and not isinstance(value, bool)
348	
349	
350	def _coordinate_pair(value: object, description: str, *, strict_list: bool) -> Position:
351	    """Validate *value* as a pair of two plain integers.
352	
353	    Booleans are rejected even though they are Python ints, and wrong lengths
354	    or element types raise :class:`ValueError` instead of leaking unpacking or
355	    hashing errors. This is the one coordinate-shape rule shared by every
356	    caller; the two entry points only differ in the outer container spellings
357	    they accept:
358	
359	    * strict JSON lists only (*strict_list* true, checkpoints, whose document
360	      shape is fixed and must not be relaxed because validation is shared);
361	    * lists or tuples alike (*strict_list* false, the direct Python interface,
362	      where the two spellings may be mixed freely).
363	    """
364	    if strict_list:
365	        # Checkpoints keep their single, fixed message for every shape problem
366	        # -- wrong type, wrong length or a non-integer (including a boolean) --
367	        # because the JSON document shape is fixed and shared validation must
368	        # not change what a malformed checkpoint reports.
369	        if (
370	            not isinstance(value, list)
371	            or len(value) != 2
372	            or not all(_is_int(coord) for coord in value)
373	        ):
374	            raise ValueError(f"{description} must be a [x, y] integer pair")
375	    else:
376	        if isinstance(value, (str, bytes)) or not isinstance(value, (tuple, list)):
377	            raise ValueError(f"{description} must be a [x, y] integer pair")
378	        if len(value) != 2:
379	            raise ValueError(f"{description} must be a [x, y] integer pair")
380	        if not all(_is_int(coord) for coord in value):
381	            raise ValueError(
382	                f"{description} coordinates must be integers, not booleans or other types"
383	            )
384	    return value[0], value[1]
385

387	def _as_cell(value: object, description: str) -> Position:
388	    """Validate a user supplied coordinate as a two-integer list or tuple."""
389	    return _coordinate_pair(value, description, strict_list=False)
390	
391	
392	def _as_pair(value: object, description: str) -> tuple[int, int]:
393	    """Validate a checkpoint coordinate as a two-integer JSON list."""
394	    return _coordinate_pair(value, description, strict_list=True)

397	def _task_route_waypoints(origin: Position, task: Task) -> list[Position]:
398	    """Required remaining visit points after *origin* for *task*.
399	
400	    The same pickup/delivery rule is used by first-time assignment, rerouting
401	    after map changes (and the recovery/sidestep planning that shares it) and
402	    checkpoint validation, so the requirement lives in exactly one place:
403	
404	    * Goods not yet collected: the route must still reach the pickup and then
405	      the dropoff. Standing exactly on the pickup makes the pickup leg empty --
406	      the leg contributes no waypoint -- but planning never collects or
407	      completes anything by itself.
408	    * Goods already collected: the robot routes straight to the dropoff, even
409	      when the old pickup cell was closed afterwards; it is never sent back.
410	
411	    When *origin*, pickup and dropoff coincide the list is empty, which
412	    describes a feasible zero-step route and must not be confused with an
413	    unreachable one.
414	    """
415	    waypoints: list[Position] = []
416	    if not task.picked_up and origin != task.pickup:
417	        waypoints.append(task.pickup)
418	    last = waypoints[-1] if waypoints else origin
419	    if task.dropoff != last:
420	        waypoints.append(task.dropoff)
421	    return waypoints

423	
424	def _plan_task_route(
425	    grid: GridMap, origin: Position, task: Task
426	) -> list[Position] | None:
427	    """Shortest feasible route through the task's required waypoints.
428	
429	    The returned list holds the cells after *origin* only, concatenating the
430	    deterministic shortest legs between consecutive required points. It is
431	    ``None`` when any required point cannot be reached, and an empty list for a
432	    feasible route with zero steps (origin already at the only destination).
433	    """
434	    route: list[Position] = []
435	    current = origin
436	    for waypoint in _task_route_waypoints(origin, task):
437	        try:
438	            leg = shortest_path(grid, current, waypoint)
439	        except ValueError:
440	            return None
441	        route.extend(leg)
442	        current = waypoint
443	    return route

446	def _validate_route_walk(
447	    grid: GridMap,
448	    origin: Position,
449	    route: Sequence[object],
450	    *,
451	    robot_id: str,
452	    checkpoint: bool,
453	    blocked_cells: frozenset[Position] | None = None,
454	) -> list[Position]:
455	    """Validate one robot's remaining route as a cell-by-cell map walk.
456	
457	    This is the single place that owns the walking rule shared by direct
458	    fleet construction and checkpoint recovery, so the same legality check is
459	    never edited twice. A route holds the cells still ahead of *origin*:
460	
461	    * every waypoint must parse as two plain integers (booleans are rejected),
462	      and lie inside the map -- a cell in *blocked_cells* is the one kind of
463	      currently obstructed waypoint a version 2 checkpoint recovery may carry
464	      (see below), everything else off the traversable map is rejected;
465	    * the first waypoint must be an up/down/left/right neighbour of *origin*,
466	      so a first waypoint equal to the current cell is rejected;
467	    * every later waypoint must be exactly one orthogonal step from the
468	      previous one -- diagonal moves, multi-cell jumps and two identical
469	      consecutive waypoints are all rejected.
470	
471	    Detours and revisits (including *origin*) are legal, and a route crossing
472	    another robot's cell is never a walk error: traffic is settled while
473	    stepping, not here. The walkability rule deliberately says nothing about
474	    the bound task's pickup/dropoff requirements; checkpoint loading keeps
475	    that separate, stricter business check. The result is a fresh mutable list
476	    of tuple cells, so validating never aliases or mutates the caller's
477	    container and a rejected input leaves every earlier object untouched.
478	
479	    *blocked_cells* is honoured only for checkpoint recovery and names the
480	    cells the recorded map-change history explains: cells open on the base map
481	    that an accepted edit has since closed and that are still closed at save
482	    time. A taskless robot's preset route may legitimately end on such a cell
483	    -- the robot keeps its unconsumed waypoints and simply waits before it --
484	    so those waypoints walk as well as the open cells do. The exemption is
485	    deliberately narrow: only checkpoint loading ever supplies the set (direct
486	    construction leaves it ``None``), only a robot without a bound task may
487	    use it (the caller never passes the set for a task route), and the cells
488	    must be inside the map -- an out-of-bounds waypoint is rejected regardless.
489	    A blocked cell in the base map that no edit explains is never part of the
490	    set, so a route crossing an initial or unexplained obstacle stays illegal.
491	
492	    The two entries keep their existing format and wording differences via
493	    *checkpoint*: direct construction (false) accepts a list or tuple route of
494	    list-or-tuple cells and reports ``route waypoint N`` with a dedicated
495	    message for a first waypoint on the current cell and for repeated
496	    consecutive waypoints; checkpoint loading (true) keeps the strict JSON
497	    list-of-lists format (``_as_pair``), says ``route entry`` and folds both
498	    equal-cell cases into its existing non-adjacency message. The checks
499	    performed are identical either way.
500	    """
501	    allowed_blocked = frozenset() if blocked_cells is None else blocked_cells
502	    waypoints: list[Position] = []
503	    previous = origin
504	    for index, cell in enumerate(route):
505	        if checkpoint:
506	            waypoint = _as_pair(
507	                cell, f"robot {robot_id!r} route entry {index}"
508	            )
509	        else:
510	            waypoint = _as_cell(
511	                cell, f"robot {robot_id!r} route waypoint {index}"
512	            )
513	        if not grid.contains(waypoint) or (
514	            waypoint in grid.obstacles and waypoint not in allowed_blocked
515	        ):
516	            if checkpoint:
517	                raise ValueError(
518	                    f"robot {robot_id!r} route entry {list(waypoint)} is "
519	                    "outside the map or inside an obstacle"
520	                )
521	            raise ValueError(
522	                f"robot {robot_id!r} route waypoint {index} "
523	                f"{list(waypoint)} is outside the map or inside an obstacle"
524	            )
525	        if waypoint == previous:
526	            if checkpoint:
527	                # The checkpoint wording treats an equal cell like any other
528	                # non-adjacent step, naming both cells of the offending move.
529	                raise ValueError(
530	                    f"robot {robot_id!r} route moves non-adjacently from "
531	                    f"{list(previous)} to {list(waypoint)}"
532	                )
533	            if index == 0:
534	                raise ValueError(
535	                    f"robot {robot_id!r} route waypoint 0 {list(waypoint)} "
536	                    "is the robot's current cell; the remaining route must "
537	                    "start with the next cell"
538	                )
539	            raise ValueError(
540	                f"robot {robot_id!r} route repeats cell {list(waypoint)} at "
541	                f"consecutive waypoints {index - 1} and {index}"
542	            )
543	        if (
544	            abs(waypoint[0] - previous[0])
545	            + abs(waypoint[1] - previous[1])
546	            != 1
547	        ):
548	            if checkpoint:
549	                raise ValueError(
550	                    f"robot {robot_id!r} route moves non-adjacently from "
551	                    f"{list(previous)} to {list(waypoint)}"
552	                )
553	            if index == 0:
554	                segment = (
555	                    f"from its current position {list(previous)} to route "
556	                    f"waypoint 0 {list(waypoint)}"
557	                )
558	            else:
559	                segment = (
560	                    f"from route waypoint {index - 1} {list(previous)} to "
561	                    f"waypoint {index} {list(waypoint)}"
562	                )
563	            raise ValueError(
564	                f"robot {robot_id!r} route moves non-adjacently {segment}: "
565	                "every step must move one orthogonal cell"
566	            )
567	        waypoints.append(waypoint)
568	        previous = waypoint
569	    return waypoints

572	def _traffic_blockers(
573	    robots: Mapping[str, Robot],
574	    paused_robots: frozenset[str] = frozenset(),
575	) -> dict[str, str]:
576	    """The robot actually holding each waitable robot's next route cell.
577	
578	    This is the single occupancy fact behind every traffic-wait judgement --
579	    tick settlement, obstacle-edit reconciliation and checkpoint validation
580	    all ask it here, so the rule is never re-derived (and never edited) in
581	    several places:
582	
583	    * a robot with no remaining route cannot be held up by traffic;
584	    * a robot paused by map unreachability cannot either -- *paused_robots*
585	      names the robots whose tasks are paused (checkpoint loading need not
586	      pass it: a paused robot's saved route is empty there, so the route
587	      check already excludes it);
588	    * otherwise the blocker is whichever robot occupies ``route[0]`` in the
589	      given layout, never the robot itself (a validated route never starts on
590	      the robot's own cell).
591	
592	    The map itself is deliberately not consulted: a next cell sealed by an
593	    obstacle alone produces no blocker -- waiting on a closure is not
594	    traffic -- and the callers own every other consequence. One cell holds at
595	    most one robot, so each waitable robot maps to at most one blocker.
596	    """
597	    occupied = {robot.position: robot.robot_id for robot in robots.values()}

599	    for robot_id, robot in robots.items():
600	        if robot_id in paused_robots or not robot.route:
601	            continue
602	        occupant_id = occupied.get(robot.route[0])
603	        if occupant_id is not None and occupant_id != robot_id:
604	            blockers[robot_id] = occupant_id

684	    @staticmethod
685	    def _require_unique_ids(
686	        robots: Sequence[Robot], tasks: Sequence[Task]
687	    ) -> None:
688	        """Reject a batch that names one robot id or task id more than once.
689	
690	        Each robot id may identify at most one robot within the given robot
691	        list, and each task id at most one task within the task list; the two
692	        namespaces are independent, so a robot and a task may share one string.
693	        The judgement is on the identifiers alone -- nothing else about two
694	        records can make a clash legal: identical records handed in twice are
695	        still duplicates, as are two robots differing only in position, idle
696	        state, preset route or in-flight task, and two tasks differing in
697	        pickup/dropoff points, owner or completion state (one finished and one
698	        still waiting included). A clash therefore never keeps one record,
699	        merges the two or renames anything: the whole request is rejected with
700	        a :class:`ValueError` that says whether the clash is among the robots
701	        or the tasks and quotes the duplicated id.
702	
703	        The check is read-only and runs before any normalization commits, so
704	        every caller object -- including records preceding a duplicate placed
705	        last -- keeps exactly the position, route containers, pickup/dropoff
706	        containers, bindings, mileage and flags it arrived with. Checkpoint
707	        loading keeps its own pre-existing duplicate rejection and wording in
708	        :meth:`_load_entities`.
709	        """
710	        seen_robot_ids: dict[str, int] = {}
711	        for index, robot in enumerate(robots):
712	            earlier = seen_robot_ids.get(robot.robot_id)
713	            if earlier is not None:
714	                raise ValueError(
715	                    f"duplicate robot id {robot.robot_id!r} in robot list: "
716	                    f"entries {earlier} and {index} both name the same robot; "
717	                    "each robot id may appear at most once in a construction "
718	                    "request"
719	                )
720	            seen_robot_ids[robot.robot_id] = index
721	        seen_task_ids: dict[str, int] = {}
722	        for index, task in enumerate(tasks):
723	            earlier = seen_task_ids.get(task.task_id)
724	            if earlier is not None:
725	                raise ValueError(
726	                    f"duplicate task id {task.task_id!r} in task list: "
727	                    f"entries {earlier} and {index} both name the same task; "
728	                    "each task id may appear at most once in a construction "
729	                    "request"
730	                )
731	            seen_task_ids[task.task_id] = index

733	    @staticmethod
734	    def _normalize_start_positions(
735	        grid: GridMap, robots: Sequence[Robot]
736	    ) -> list[Position]:
737	        """Validate every robot's starting position and return tuple copies.
738	
739	        The position rule is deliberately the same strict rule the route
740	        waypoints use (:func:`_as_cell`): a position must be a list or tuple
741	        (the two spellings may be mixed across one batch) holding exactly two
742	        plain integers -- booleans are rejected even though they are Python
743	        ints, and floats, strings, missing components, extra components and
744	        non-pair inputs are all refused with :class:`ValueError` naming the
745	        robot and its bad position, never rounded, coerced or padded.
746	
747	        Every accepted position is additionally checked against the map: it
748	        must lie inside the grid and outside every obstacle. Two robots may
749	        not start on the same cell either; the comparison runs on normalized
750	        tuple values, so one robot spelling a cell as ``[x, y]`` and another
751	        as ``(x, y)`` is still a collision, and the error names both robots
752	        involved. Idle robots, task-bound robots and robots carrying preset
753	        routes are all checked -- no robot is skipped to make a batch pass.
754	
755	        The check is read-only: it returns a fresh tuple per robot and commits
756	        nothing itself. The caller assigns the tuples to the robots only once
757	        the whole batch (routes and task bindings included) has passed, so a
758	        later rejection leaves the caller's positions untouched, and the tuple
759	        copy means mutating an originally passed-in list after construction
760	        can never change the created fleet.
761	        """
762	        normalized: list[Position] = []
763	        occupied: dict[Position, str] = {}
764	        for robot in robots:
765	            position = _as_cell(
766	                robot.position, f"robot {robot.robot_id!r} starting position"
767	            )
768	            if not grid.traversable(position):
769	                raise ValueError(
770	                    f"robot {robot.robot_id!r} starting position {list(position)} "
771	                    "is outside the map or inside an obstacle"
772	                )
773	            other_id = occupied.get(position)
774	            if other_id is not None:
775	                raise ValueError(
776	                    f"robot {robot.robot_id!r} starting position {list(position)} "
777	                    f"is already occupied by robot {other_id!r}: robots cannot "
778	                    "share an initial cell"
779	                )
780	            occupied[position] = robot.robot_id
781	            normalized.append(position)
782	        return normalized

784	    @staticmethod
785	    def _normalize_task_coordinates(
786	        tasks: Sequence[Task],
787	    ) -> list[tuple[Position, Position]]:
788	        """Validate every task's pickup and dropoff and return tuple copies.
789	
790	        Task points share the strict position rule (:func:`_as_cell`): each one
791	        must be a list or tuple (the two spellings may be mixed within one
792	        task and across one batch) holding exactly two plain integers --
793	        booleans are rejected even though they are Python ints, and floats
794	        (even ``1.0``), strings, nulls, missing components, extra components
795	        and non-pair inputs are all refused with :class:`ValueError` naming the
796	        task and whether its pickup or its dropoff is at fault, never rounded,
797	        padded or coerced. This runs for every task regardless of state --
798	        waiting for assignment, en route to pickup, already carrying the goods
799	        or already completed -- so a malformed point in a finished historical
800	        record is refused at construction just like one in a pending task.
801	
802	        Coordinate validity is deliberately kept separate from reachability:
803	        whether a robot can currently reach the points is never judged here, so
804	        a well-formed task whose pickup is currently unreachable keeps waiting
805	        exactly as before, and a loaded task whose pickup cell has since been
806	        closed keeps the goods and its binding -- neither is an error.
807	
808	        The check is read-only: it returns a fresh integer tuple per point and
809	        commits nothing itself. The caller assigns the tuples to the tasks only
810	        once the whole batch (positions, ownership and routes included) has
811	        passed, so a later rejection leaves the caller's tasks holding their
812	        original pickup/dropoff containers, and the tuple copy means mutating
813	        an originally passed-in list after construction can never change the
814	        created fleet. A list and a tuple naming one cell normalize to equal
815	        tuples, so they can never make a robot miss a pickup or fail a delivery
816	        merely because of the container type.
817	        """
818	        normalized: list[tuple[Position, Position]] = []
819	        for task in tasks:
820	            pickup = _as_cell(task.pickup, f"task {task.task_id!r} pickup")

825	    @staticmethod
826	    def _validate_task_ownership(robots: Sequence[Robot], tasks: Sequence[Task]) -> None:
827	        """Reject impossible initial bindings between robots and tasks.
828	
829	        The very same ownership requirements back direct construction and
830	        checkpoint loading, so they live in exactly one place. The mutual
831	        binding only governs work still in progress:
832	
833	        * A robot that declares a task must name a task that exists, is not
834	          completed yet, and is assigned back to that same robot.
835	        * An unfinished task that names an owner must name an existing robot
836	          whose current task it is; an unfinished task with the goods already
837	          collected additionally must have an owner.
838	        * A robot can therefore never be claimed by two unfinished tasks: the
839	          second task's owner points at a robot that executes another task.
840	        * A completed task must carry the picked-up mark *and* a historical
841	          owner (a non-null ``assigned_robot``); see below.
842	
843	        Completed tasks are history, not work in progress, but the history must
844	        still be coherent: a finished task must carry both the picked-up mark
845	        and the id of the robot that finished it -- ``None`` means "no record",
846	        never an anonymous completion, even when the pickup point and the
847	        dropoff coincide. Neither gap is repaired (the owner is not filled in,
848	        the pickup mark is not flipped, nothing is reassigned or dropped); the
849	        fleet is rejected as a whole with a :class:`ValueError` naming the task
850	        and the exact contradiction. The historical owner itself is bound by
851	        none of the in-progress rules: it need not be idle or name the task
852	        back, may already work a new task, may have finished several tasks, and
853	        may even be absent from the fleet, so historical records never occupy a
854	        robot or take part in new task assignment. Unassigned, not-yet-collected
855	        tasks simply wait -- even when no robot can reach them -- and are not an
856	        ownership error. Nothing here rewrites a binding or drops a task; an
857	        inconsistent input is rejected as a whole, leaving the caller's objects
858	        untouched.
859	        """
860	        robot_by_id = {robot.robot_id: robot for robot in robots}
861	        task_by_id = {task.task_id: task for task in tasks}
862	        for robot in robots:
863	            if robot.task_id is None:
864	                continue
865	            task = task_by_id.get(robot.task_id)
866	            if task is None:
867	                raise ValueError(
868	                    f"robot {robot.robot_id!r} executes unknown task "
869	                    f"{robot.task_id!r}"
870	                )
871	            if task.completed:
872	                raise ValueError(
873	                    f"robot {robot.robot_id!r} executes task {task.task_id!r} "
874	                    "that is already completed"
875	                )
876	            if task.assigned_robot != robot.robot_id:
877	                raise ValueError(
878	                    f"robot {robot.robot_id!r} executes task {task.task_id!r} "
879	                    f"but the task is assigned to {task.assigned_robot!r}"
880	                )
881	        for task in tasks:
882	            if task.completed:
883	                # A finished task is a fixed historical record: the goods must
884	                # have been collected and a historical finishing robot must be
885	                # named. The very same requirement backs direct construction
886	                # and checkpoint recovery, so a document that could never be
887	                # loaded again can never be built in the first place. This is
888	                # judged purely from the record -- even a task whose pickup
889	                # point equals its dropoff is not presumed collected -- and the
890	                # recorded robot is history only: it is never looked up, so it
891	                # may be retired, idle or already busy with another task, and
892	                # several completed tasks may name the same robot without ever
893	                # counting as occupying it.
894	                if not task.picked_up:
895	                    if task.assigned_robot is None:
896	                        raise ValueError(
897	                            f"task {task.task_id!r} is marked completed but was "
898	                            "never picked up and has no historical assigned robot"
899	                        )
900	                    raise ValueError(
901	                        f"task {task.task_id!r} is marked completed but never "
902	                        "picked up, even though historical robot "
903	                        f"{task.assigned_robot!r} is recorded for it"
904	                    )
905	                if task.assigned_robot is None:
906	                    raise ValueError(
907	                        f"task {task.task_id!r} is marked completed and picked up "
908	                        "but has no historical assigned robot"
909	                    )
910	                continue
911	            if task.picked_up and task.assigned_robot is None:
912	                raise ValueError(
913	                    f"task {task.task_id!r} is picked up but has no assigned robot"
914	                )
915	            if task.assigned_robot is not None:
916	                owner = robot_by_id.get(task.assigned_robot)
917	                if owner is None:
918	                    raise ValueError(
919	                        f"task {task.task_id!r} is assigned to unknown robot "
920	                        f"{task.assigned_robot!r}"
921	                    )
922	                if owner.task_id != task.task_id:
923	                    raise ValueError(
924	                        f"task {task.task_id!r} claims robot {owner.robot_id!r} "
925	                        f"but the robot executes {owner.task_id!r}"
926	                    )

928	    @staticmethod
929	    def _normalize_initial_routes(
930	        grid: GridMap,
931	        robots: Sequence[Robot],
932	        positions: Sequence[Position],
933	    ) -> list[list[Position]]:
934	        """Validate every remaining route and return normalized copies.
935	
936	        Every robot is checked, idle or task-bound, via the single shared walk
937	        validator :func:`_validate_route_walk` -- the same coordinate shape,
938	        map-walkability and one-orthogonal-step rule checkpoint recovery uses
939	        -- so a walking rule never has to be changed in two places. The outer
940	        route may be a list or tuple and each waypoint may itself be a list or
941	        tuple of two plain integers -- booleans are not integers here, and
942	        wrong lengths or element types raise :class:`ValueError` instead of
943	        leaking unpacking or hashing failures. The forms may be mixed freely;
944	        only the coordinate order matters, not the container types.
945	
946	        *positions* holds the already-normalized tuple starting positions from
947	        :meth:`_normalize_start_positions`, paired one-to-one with *robots*:
948	        every route is walked from the tuple form so a first waypoint equal to
949	        the start cell is recognized regardless of how the caller spelled
950	        either container.
951	
952	        Accepted routes are returned as mutable lists of tuple cells, the one
953	        shape the rest of the engine relies on (head consumption with
954	        ``pop(0)`` and hashable cells for road and occupancy checks). Empty
955	        lists and tuples both normalize to an empty route. Routes need not be
956	        shortest paths and may revisit cells, and traffic (a route crossing
957	        another robot's cell, or routes sharing a cell) is left to execution:
958	        only walkability on the given map is judged.
959	
960	        The check is read-only -- :func:`_validate_route_walk` builds fresh
961	        lists, and the caller commits them itself only once every robot has
962	        passed, so a rejected fleet is rejected as a whole: an error on a
963	        later robot or at the end of a route never truncates, pads, reorders
964	        or otherwise modifies an earlier robot or any caller object. The
965	        shared walk check says nothing about tasks; direct construction keeps
966	        accepting any walkable route, while checkpoint loading keeps its own
967	        stricter validation that also covers the pickup/dropoff rules.
968	        """
969	        normalized: list[list[Position]] = []
970	        for robot, position in zip(robots, positions):
971	            route = robot.route
972	            if not isinstance(route, (list, tuple)):
973	                raise ValueError(
974	                    f"robot {robot.robot_id!r} remaining route must be a list "
975	                    "of [x, y] waypoints"
976	                )
977	            normalized.append(
978	                _validate_route_walk(
979	                    grid,
980	                    position,
981	                    route,
982	                    robot_id=robot.robot_id,
983	                    checkpoint=False,
984	                )
985	            )
986	        return normalized

992	    def modify_obstacles(
993	        self,
994	        added: Sequence[Position] = (),
995	        removed: Sequence[Position] = (),
996	    ) -> dict[str, object]:
997	        """Close and/or reopen cells without advancing the simulation.
998	
999	        The whole request is validated before anything changes: coordinates
1000	        must be two plain integers (booleans are rejected), lie inside the
1001	        map, no cell may appear in both lists, and newly added obstacles may
1002	        not cover a robot's current cell. Duplicate coordinates inside one
1003	        batch are processed once. Adding an existing obstacle or removing a
1004	        traversable cell is a no-op. Invalid requests raise :class:`ValueError`
1005	        and leave every part of the state untouched.
1006	
1007	        Assigned unfinished tasks keep their robot: routes are replanned
1008	        against the new map, or, when a required point is unreachable, cleared
1009	        while the task is suspended. No tick is recorded, no robot moves and no
1010	        distance is accumulated.
1011	        """
1012	        add_cells = self._normalize_cells(added, "added")
1013	        remove_cells = self._normalize_cells(removed, "removed")
1014	        conflict = set(add_cells) & set(remove_cells)
1015	        if conflict:
1016	            cell = sorted(conflict)[0]
1017	            raise ValueError(
1018	                f"cell {list(cell)} is both added and removed in the same request"
1019	            )
1020	        occupied = {robot.position for robot in self.robots.values()}
1021	        for cell in add_cells:
1022	            if cell in occupied:
1023	                raise ValueError(
1024	                    f"cannot add obstacle at {list(cell)}: a robot currently occupies it"
1025	                )
1026	        return self._apply_map_change(add_cells, remove_cells)
1027	
1028	    def _normalize_cells(self, cells: Sequence[Position], label: str) -> list[Position]:
1029	        if isinstance(cells, (str, bytes)) or not isinstance(cells, (list, tuple)):
1030	            raise ValueError(f"{label} cells must be provided as a list of [x, y] pairs")
1031	        seen: set[Position] = set()
1032	        ordered: list[Position] = []
1033	        for index, cell in enumerate(cells):
1034	            position = _as_cell(cell, f"{label} cell {index}")
1035	            if not self.grid.contains(position):
1036	                raise ValueError(f"{label} cell {list(position)} lies outside the map")
1037	            if position in seen:
1038	                # Batch-internal duplicates are handled once, not rejected.
1039	                continue
1040	            seen.add(position)
1041	            ordered.append(position)
1042	        return ordered
1043	
1044	    def _apply_map_change(
1045	        self, added: list[Position], removed: list[Position]
1046	    ) -> dict[str, object]:
1047	        obstacles = set(self.grid.obstacles)
1048	        actual_added = [cell for cell in added if cell not in obstacles]
1049	        obstacles.update(actual_added)
1050	        actual_removed = [cell for cell in removed if cell in obstacles]
1051	        obstacles.difference_update(actual_removed)
1052	        if not actual_added and not actual_removed:
1053	            return self._map_change_record(self._map_sequence, [], [])
1054	
1055	        # Everything below only runs once the batch was fully validated and is
1056	        # known to change the map.
1057	        self.grid = GridMap(self.grid.width, self.grid.height, frozenset(obstacles))
1058	        self._map_sequence += 1
1059	        record = self._map_change_record(self._map_sequence, actual_added, actual_removed)
1060	        self.map_changes.append(copy.deepcopy(record))
1061	        self.replay.append(copy.deepcopy(record))
1062	        self._reroute_after_map_change()
1063	        self._reconcile_traffic_waits_after_map_change()
1064	        return copy.deepcopy(record)
1065	
1066	    def _map_change_record(
1067	        self, sequence: int, added: list[Position], removed: list[Position]
1068	    ) -> dict[str, object]:
1069	        return {
1070	            "type": "map_change",
1071	            "tick": self.tick,
1072	            "sequence": sequence,
1073	            "added": [list(cell) for cell in added],
1074	            "removed": [list(cell) for cell in removed],
1075	        }

1077	    def _plan_route(
1078	        self, robot: Robot, task: Task, start: Position | None = None
1079	    ) -> list[Position] | None:
1080	        """Shortest current->pickup->dropoff route, or None if unreachable.
1081	
1082	        *start* overrides the robot's current position, which is how sidestep
1083	        candidates are evaluated without moving the robot first. The
1084	        pickup/delivery rule itself is shared with first-time assignment and
1085	        checkpoint validation via :func:`_plan_task_route`.
1086	        """
1087	        origin = robot.position if start is None else start
1088	        return _plan_task_route(self.grid, origin, task)

"""Task assignment, dynamic map edits and collision-aware tick execution.

Obstacles may be closed and reopened between ticks through
:meth:`FleetSimulator.modify_obstacles`. Every accepted edit is appended to a
deterministic change history and mirrored into the replay as a ``map_change``
event stamped with the tick at which it took effect. Tick frames themselves are
never rewritten, so historical frames keep the positions and completion
information recorded at the time.

Automatic yielding
------------------
When a robot's next waypoint is occupied by another robot, ``step()`` tries to
keep traffic flowing instead of waiting forever: a parked blocker (one with no
bound task *and* no remaining route) is asked to move onto a free side cell
that lies on no robot's planned route, and a busy robot facing a blocker that
cannot drive on may itself sidestep onto a free adjacent cell and replan its
(still shortest) route from there. A taskless robot that still carries a
remaining route is not parked: it drives that route cell by cell exactly like
a task-bound robot, is never pushed onto a side cell for someone else, and if
its own next cell is blocked it simply keeps its place and its unconsumed
waypoints -- an open side cell changes nothing. Only once such a route is
exhausted does the robot become a parked robot and yield by the side-cell
rule. Task assignment follows the same line: only a robot with no bound task
*and* no remaining route can receive a waiting task, so a taskless robot
still driving its preset route never has that route overwritten by a new
assignment -- being blocked by traffic along the way does not count as having
finished the route, and once the route runs out the robot joins the selection
at the next assignment pass, planned from wherever it stands then. A retreat that
only leads back to the same immovable blocker is never taken though: if the
replanned route immediately returns through the vacated cell, still passes the
blocker's cell and the blocker cannot use the opening to leave (a dead end or
corridor end with traffic parked beyond it), the robot simply waits -- extra
empty cells stretching out behind it change nothing. Nor does the blocker's
own side step automatically count as leaving: when that step only moves the
blocker onto a side cell whose replanned route returns it onto the corridor
to face the very same unyielding jam further ahead, the opening is no opening
and the retreat behind it is rejected as well. Yield moves count as
mileage, waiting does not. The task keeps its original robot, pickup and
completion rules are unchanged, and a robot paused by map unreachability never
takes part in yielding. If no safe side cell exists the robots simply wait:
time advances, nothing collides and nothing completes early. Waiting caused
purely by other robots is tracked per robot (consecutive ticks and the
blocking robot) and reported by :meth:`FleetSimulator.status` and
:meth:`FleetSimulator.metrics` as ``traffic_waits``, distinct from the
map-unreachability ``paused_tasks``. The record is judged against the
end-of-tick layout, not the moment the robot gave way: when a robot that was
asked to wait sees its next cell free at tick end (the blocker drove on or
made room later in the same tick), no wait is reported for that tick at all,
and ``blocked_by`` names whichever robot actually occupies the cell once the
tick settles. The counter clears the moment the robot moves again or the
blockage ends; an uninterrupted wait whose blocking robot merely changes
identity keeps accumulating with the new blocker, whereas a wait that was
interrupted and later recurs starts again at one. An accepted map edit
reconciles the records immediately: a robot paused by the new map or no
longer facing its recorded blocker on the replanned route loses its entry, an
entry still facing the same blocker keeps its count, and no edit ever creates
or increments one.

Initial identifiers
-------------------
Identity is per batch and per kind: each robot id may name at most one robot
in the robot list and each task id at most one task in the task list, while
the two lists have independent namespaces -- a robot and a task may share one
string, a task's owner reference is not a second robot record, and any number
of completed tasks may keep the same historical robot, even one absent from
the fleet. The identifier alone decides: identical objects passed twice, two
robots that differ only in position, idle state, preset route or current task,
and two tasks that differ in pickup/dropoff, owner or completion (one already
finished beside one still waiting) are all rejected. Nothing keeps one copy,
merges the records or renames them -- the whole request raises
:class:`ValueError` saying whether the clash is in the robots or the tasks and
quoting the duplicated id. The check is read-only and runs before any
normalization commits, so even a duplicate at the end of either list leaves
every earlier object -- positions, list-shaped routes and points, bindings,
mileage and flags -- exactly as supplied; tasks distinct in id but equal in
pickup/dropoff stay distinct records and both take part in assignment and
completion statistics. Checkpoint files keep their own pre-existing duplicate
id rejection unchanged.

Initial task ownership
----------------------
A fleet can be created mid-work: a robot may already name its current task
with a remaining route, and a task may already be assigned or even loaded.
Construction validates these bindings up front instead of discovering them
while stepping. Every robot that names a task must name one that exists, is
still unfinished and is assigned back to that robot; every unfinished task
that names an owner must name an existing robot whose current task it is, and
a task with the goods collected may never lack that owner. One robot is
therefore never claimed by two unfinished tasks, and a robot may never be
bound to a completed task. A finished task is a fixed historical record and
must carry both the picked-up mark and the historical robot that finished it:
``assigned_robot`` of ``None`` means the record is missing, not an anonymous
completion, and the mark is never presumed -- not even when the task's pickup
point and dropoff are the same cell. Finished tasks only retain *historical*
ownership: their recorded robot need not be idle or name them back, may
already work a new task, may have finished several tasks, and may even be
absent from the fleet, so history never occupies a robot or enters new task
assignment. Unassigned, not-yet-collected tasks simply wait -- including ones
no robot can currently reach -- and are not an ownership error. Conflicts
raise :class:`ValueError` naming the robot or task and the contradiction
involved; nothing is rebound, unassigned or dropped, and the caller's objects
are left untouched. The very same ownership and completed-history rules
govern checkpoint loading, so a completion record one entry point accepts
can never be a record the other cannot reload.

Every task's pickup point and dropoff is validated with the very same strict
coordinate rule as robot positions (:func:`_as_cell`): each must be a list or
tuple holding exactly two plain integers, and the two spellings may be mixed
freely within one task and across one batch. A boolean is never an integer
here -- not even ``True`` for a 1-coordinate -- and a float is refused even
when it equals an integer value such as ``1.0``; strings, nulls, scalars,
missing components, extra components and anything that is not a coordinate
pair all raise :class:`ValueError` naming the task id and whether its pickup
or its dropoff is at fault -- nothing is rounded, padded or coerced into a
pair, so a fleet can never accept a task that its own checkpoint loading
would later reject. An accepted point is normalized to a fresh integer tuple
(``[1, 0]`` and ``(1, 0)`` therefore name one cell: a robot can neither miss
a pickup nor fail a delivery merely because the containers differ), and the
copy means a caller that keeps mutating its original coordinate lists after
construction can never change the created fleet. The rule covers every task
regardless of state -- waiting for assignment, already assigned and heading
to pickup, carrying the goods, and finished historical records alike. Like
position normalization, the points commit nothing until the whole batch
(positions, ownership, routes and all task points) has passed: a failure on a
later task point, robot route or binding leaves every earlier task holding
its original pickup/dropoff containers and every flag, binding, route and
mileage exactly as passed in. Coordinate validity and current reachability
are deliberately separate judgements: a well-formed task no robot can
currently reach simply keeps waiting, and a loaded task whose pickup cell has
since been closed keeps the goods and its owner -- neither is a coordinate
error, and selection order, planning, obstacle handling and completion
history behave exactly as before. Checkpoints keep their integer coordinate
arrays and strict loading rules unchanged -- no format bump and no
relaxation.

Every robot's starting position is validated with the very same strict
coordinate rule its route waypoints use (:func:`_as_cell`): it must be a list
or tuple holding exactly two plain integers, and the two spellings may be
mixed freely within one batch. A boolean is never an integer here, and floats,
strings, missing or extra components and anything that is not a coordinate
pair all raise :class:`ValueError` naming the robot and its offending starting
position -- nothing is rounded, coerced or padded into a pair. An accepted
position is normalized to a fresh integer tuple (``[0, 0]`` and ``(0, 0)``
therefore create identical fleets that move and receive tasks identically),
and the copy means a caller that keeps mutating its original list after
construction can never change the created fleet. Positions must lie inside
the map and outside every obstacle, and no two robots may start on the same
cell: the comparison is made on the normalized coordinate values, so a list
and a tuple naming one cell still collide, and the error names both robots.
This covers every robot regardless of task state -- unbound, task-executing
and preset-route robots alike -- so a batch can never succeed by ignoring one
robot. Like the route check, position normalization commits nothing until the
entire batch (positions, ownership and routes) has passed: a failure on a
later robot's route or task binding leaves every earlier robot's original
position object, remaining route and task binding exactly as passed in.

Every robot's remaining route is also validated as a walk on the given map,
whether or not the robot is bound to a task, and direct construction and
checkpoint recovery run the *same* :func:`_validate_route_walk` check, so the
walking rule is maintained in exactly one place. The route omits the robot's
current cell, so a non-empty route must begin with an up/down/left/right
neighbour of that cell and every later waypoint must be one orthogonal step
from the previous one; each waypoint must be in bounds and free of obstacles.
Diagonal steps, multi-cell jumps, two identical consecutive waypoints and a
first waypoint equal to the current position are all rejected, and waypoints
must be two plain integers (never booleans) in a list or tuple, with wrong
lengths or element types raising :class:`ValueError` rather than leaking
unpacking or hashing errors. Empty routes stay legal; a route need not be
shortest and may revisit cells. A route crossing another robot's current cell,
or several robots planning through the same cell, is not an error -- those
traffic conflicts are settled during execution. The direct interface keeps
its existing acceptance of a bound route's pickup/dropoff ordering and end
point; checkpoint loading additionally keeps its own stricter route checks
(including the task completion rules), its format and the map-paused
behaviour, under which a paused robot resumes with an empty route.

Direct construction always judges every waypoint against the map handed to
it, so a route crossing an initial obstacle is rejected no matter the robot's
task state. Checkpoint recovery owns exactly one relaxation, and only for a
version 2 document: a robot with no bound task keeps its remaining preset
waypoints when a later map edit closes the cell ahead -- it simply waits
before it -- so such a waypoint may be blocked on the saved map provided it
was traversable on the base map, some recorded change net-closes it and it is
still closed at save time. The set of cells this can possibly cover is
derived from the already validated ``base_grid`` plus ``map_changes``, never
from the route itself: a base-map obstacle and any blocked cell the history
cannot explain stay rejected, version 1 files (which carry no history) keep
the old rule, and a task-bound robot never qualifies. Out-of-bounds,
malformed and non-adjacent waypoints are rejected for every robot either
way. After reopening, the restored robot keeps driving the same cells in the
same order: waiting neither consumes a waypoint nor adds mileage, and the
route is never replanned into a shortcut.

Checkpoint file format
----------------------
``save_checkpoint`` writes versioned, UTF-8 encoded JSON. The current format
version is ``2``; version ``1`` files remain readable.

``version``
    Integer format version (``1`` or ``2``).
``grid``
    ``{"width": int, "height": int, "obstacles": [[x, y], ...]}`` describing
    the map dimensions and every currently blocked cell.
``tick``
    Non-negative integer: the number of ticks already executed. Saving and
    loading never advance this value.
``robots``
    List of robot states, each
    ``{"robot_id": str, "position": [x, y], "route": [[x, y], ...],
    "task_id": str | null, "distance_travelled": int}``. ``route`` holds the
    remaining waypoints after ``position`` (empty for a paused robot). For a
    taskless robot the route may head into a cell the change history has
    closed and the saved grid still shows blocked: the robot is simply waiting
    there with its preset waypoints intact, and loading restores that wait.
``tasks``
    List of task states, each
    ``{"task_id": str, "pickup": [x, y], "dropoff": [x, y],
    "assigned_robot": str | null, "picked_up": bool, "completed": bool}``.
    Completed tasks keep their historical ``assigned_robot``: a task saved as
    completed must also be marked picked up and name the robot that finished
    it (never null), and loading rejects a record missing either half with the
    same rule direct fleet construction enforces.
``replay``
    Ordered event list. Tick events are numbered consecutively from ``1``
    through ``tick`` and have the shape
    ``{"type": "tick", "tick": int, "moved": [robot_id, ...],
    "robots": {robot_id: [x, y], ...}, "completed": [task_id, ...]}``.
    ``completed`` is the cumulative set of tasks finished by the end of that
    tick: entries must name checkpoint tasks without repeats within one frame,
    a recorded completion must survive every later frame, and the final
    frame's set must equal the tasks saved with ``completed: true``.
    Map-change events sit between ticks (or after the last tick) and look like
    ``{"type": "map_change", "tick": int, "sequence": int,
    "added": [[x, y], ...], "removed": [[x, y], ...]}``. When ``tick`` is
    non-zero the final tick event's robot positions must match the current
    robot positions.
``map_changes`` (version 2 only)
    List mirroring the replay map-change events in the same order:
    ``{"tick": int, "sequence": int, "added": [...], "removed": [...]}``.
``base_grid`` (version 2 only)
    ``{"width", "height", "obstacles"}`` describing the map before any runtime
    edit. Replaying ``map_changes`` against it must reproduce the saved current
    ``grid``.
``traffic_waits`` (optional)
    List of ``{"robot_id": str, "blocked_by": [str, ...], "ticks": int}``
    entries recording how many consecutive ticks each robot has been held up
    purely by other robots. Absent in older files, which load with every
    wait counter at zero. Each entry must agree with the saved layout: the
    robot needs a remaining route and ``blocked_by`` must name exactly the
    robot occupying its next route cell -- a next cell nobody occupies, a
    listed blocker parked elsewhere, or extra names beside the real blocker
    all reject the document.

Version 1 documents store tick frames without a ``type`` field and have no
``map_changes`` or ``base_grid`` key; they load with their grid taken as the
baseline, as if no map edit ever happened.

The ordinary-tick-frame rules both versions share -- the replay container is
a list, every frame is an object, and tick frames are numbered consecutively
from 1 with a well-formed payload -- are owned by the single shared
:meth:`FleetSimulator._iter_replay_events` scan, so they are maintained in
exactly one place. Each version keeps its own handling on top: version 1
rejects non-tick frames and fills in the missing ``type`` on a copy, while
version 2 dispatches event types and enforces its map-change ordering.

Both map definitions are validated by the single shared
:meth:`FleetSimulator._load_map_definition` rule -- positive integer
dimensions, an obstacle list of integer ``[x, y]`` pairs inside the map --
with wording that names the map at fault, so a format or value rule is
maintained in exactly one place while each map keeps its own contents. The
cross-definition constraints (matching dimensions and a history that replays
``base_grid`` onto ``grid``) are checked separately and remain distinct
rejection reasons from a malformed definition.

Loading performs strict validation: malformed JSON, missing or wrongly typed
fields, unsupported versions, duplicate or inconsistent entities, out of
bounds/obstructed positions and routes, non-adjacent route steps, ownership
mismatches, routes that cannot finish the robot's bound task, traffic waits
that contradict the saved robot positions and remaining routes, broken replay
or map-change history, a completion history that contradicts the saved task
states, and a history that does not reproduce the saved grid all raise
:class:`ValueError`.

The single route-walk exception recovery allows is a preset-route robot that
is waiting out a dynamic closure. In a version 2 file a robot without a bound
task may keep waypoints that are blocked on the saved grid when the base map
had the cell open and the recorded change history explains its current,
still-effective closure (a cell closed and reopened before the save is open
again and therefore never covered). Such a robot was produced by normal
running -- closing a cell never strips a taskless robot of its remaining
route, the robot just waits before the cell -- so recovery restores it as is
and it drives on, same cells, same order, once the cell reopens. The
exemption cannot reach anything else: direct fleet construction has no
history and rejects routes through initial obstacles, a blocked waypoint the
history cannot account for (including every blocked waypoint in a version 1
document) is still rejected, and robots bound to a task never qualify --
their routes are replanned or their tasks paused at edit time and load under
the unchanged task rules. A robot standing on an obstacle and an out-of-map,
malformed or non-adjacent waypoint are rejected regardless of task state.

A task-bound route is judged against the task's pickup state, not just for
walkability. For every assigned, unfinished task that is not paused by map
unreachability, a non-empty remaining route must end at the dropoff, and when
the goods are not yet collected and the robot is not already standing on the
pickup cell, the route must still pass through that pickup cell -- passing the
dropoff early changes nothing as long as the route later collects and returns,
and avoidance detours need not match a replanned shortest route. An empty
route is accepted only when a loaded robot already stands at the dropoff, or
when position, pickup and dropoff all coincide; paused tasks keep their
empty-route exemption, and unassigned or completed tasks are not checked.

The recorded movement history is checked for physical plausibility, not just
for a matching final frame. In every tick frame each robot must stand on a
cell that is in bounds and traversable on the map of that moment, no two
robots may end a tick on the same cell, and from the second frame on a robot
may only have waited or stepped one orthogonal cell (two robots cannot swap
cells within one tick; following a robot into the cell it just vacated is
fine). A frame's ``moved`` list must reference current fleet robots without
duplicates and, whenever a previous frame exists, must name exactly the
robots whose positions changed, in any order. Version 2 map changes are
applied in their recorded order after the tick they are stamped on, so a
robot may be recorded in a cell that is closed later, may not appear in a
cell before it opens, and no change may add an obstacle onto a cell a tick
frame shows occupied -- not even when a later change of the same tick removes
it. Filesystem and permission failures propagate as :class:`OSError`.
"""
